note: This is the last commit confirmed live in production as of this deploy. Update this file after every deploy made THROUGH this pipeline, so the next build's manifest.previous_commit is accurate.
migrations_applied: None. migrate-check reported pending_migrations_detected false and 'Nothing to migrate' — this release carries only resources/css/provatferi-admin.css (brand accent-color for checkboxes/radios outside .form-check, the indeterminate state, a legible disabled state, and resize: none on textareas). No PHP, route or schema change.
switch_note: Clean switch, unlike the previous release: ok:true, atomic_rename_ms 0.261, public assets synced in 3.3ms, and the in-process cache rebuild completed (config:clear/view:clear/config:cache/view:cache all exit 0). route:cache was correctly SKIPPED because routes/ was unchanged from the previous release — that is the tool's own optimisation, not a missed step. No repair script was needed this time.
switch_rename_anomaly: HISTORICAL (release eea9a61dc7c7-2026-09-1711033): `switch` reported {ok:false, error:'atomic rename failed', renamed_old:true, renamed_new:false} while the second rename HAD taken effect — the new tree was already live and serving. The script's revert was correctly skipped because it only reverts when laravel-admin is missing. Consequence then: switch aborted before its cache rebuild and bookkeeping, which a one-off script completed. If this recurs: do NOT re-run switch blindly — first check whether the live tree is already the new release (the API contract or a file probe is the fastest tell), because a second switch would rotate a healthy release out.
switch_gate_note: release-manager.php `switch` requires stage/build/contract_check/smoke_test_isolated but NOT migrate_apply, even when migrate-check reported pending migrations. Always read migrate-check and run migrate-apply before scheduling switch; never pre-schedule switch on a release that carries migrations.
upload_url_note: Generate the TUS upload URL for provatferi.org and point HOSTINGER_UPLOAD_URL at .../api/tus/public_html/admin. A URL whose root is public_html alone stages the release into the MAIN site's web root instead. The file-browser session behind a generated URL can expire well before its token's exp (a 2h-old one returned 403 on 2026-09-14) — regenerate if an upload is refused. A TUS upload can also return 204 with the right Upload-Offset and still not persist the file (observed 2026-09-17 with _diag.php and again with _qa_cleanup.php); re-uploading under a FRESH filename worked both times. Always confirm a one-off script exists via the file listing before relying on it, since a missing file and the CLI guard both answer 404 over HTTP.
cron_invocation_note: Invoke as `/usr/bin/php /home/u951246149/domains/provatferi.org/laravel-admin-releases/_tooling/release-manager.php <cmd> <releaseId> 2>&1`, one command per cron. The `cd <tooling> && php release-manager.php ...` form produced no output and did not run on this host. A cron command containing a quoted `php -r` one-liner was rejected by the hosting API (empty uid returned) — upload a small script and invoke it by absolute path instead. Delete each one-shot cron as soon as its output is read; a `switch` cron left armed would rotate directories again on the next minute.
maintenance_script_note: Any one-off PHP script uploaded to public_html/admin that bootstraps Laravel from absolute paths WILL execute when requested over HTTP, not only via cron. Guard such scripts with `if (PHP_SAPI !== 'cli') { http_response_code(404); exit; }` before uploading, and have them @unlink(__FILE__) when done. A self-deleting script means the NEXT cron firing logs 'Could not open input file' — expected, not a failure — but it also means the script's output must be read before that second firing, or the audit dump is lost (this happened once on 2026-09-17).
manual_sync_required: NOT applicable any more for provatferi-admin.css: it is compiled through Vite (resources/css/provatferi-admin.css -> public/build) and is covered by deploy/asset-contract.php, so it ships inside the release artifact.
